title: Follow-up: could IBKR ever supply swing-mode's daily/weekly OHLCV, and should it?
description:
backend-portfolio-load-performance investigated the user's 'can it be faster when using ibkr as much as possible if ibkr is connected' request and found that `IBKRProvider` (app/data/ibkr_provider.py) cannot currently supply a daily/weekly-OHLCV-shaped fetch matching the swing `DataProvider` protocol (`get_daily_ohlcv`/`get_weekly_ohlcv`): its only market-data method is `get_hourly_bars` (native intraday granularity, ~833-day pagination ceiling at the default `'1h'` bar size), with no existing resample-to-daily/weekly pipeline for it. That parent task's own `decisions` entry has the full investigation detail.

This follow-up exists to hold that larger, two-part question for whoever picks it up next, WITHOUT assuming either part's answer:

1. **Is building an IBKR-backed daily/weekly-shaped fetch even worth doing?** It would mean a new `IBKRProvider` method (or a small adapter over `get_hourly_bars` + a resampling pass, mirroring `app.data.day_trader_intraday`'s existing hourly-to-target-interval resampling via `app.data.base.resample_ohlcv`), PLUS a design decision on `get_hourly_bars`' own ~833-day lookback ceiling being far short of what swing-mode signal computation reads in practice (well beyond `YFinanceProvider._MIN_WEEKLY_BARS = 26` weekly bars' bare minimum) -- a resampled-from-hourly daily/weekly series would have much less history than yfinance/Stooq's `period='max'` fetch, which could itself degrade signal quality (e.g. Screen 1/Tide's own EMA/MACD warm-up) even if it were faster.

2. **If it is worth building, should swing mode actually USE it when IBKR is connected?** This directly touches the already-established, explicitly-documented precedent that `current_price`/`unrealized_pnl_pct`/`equity` are 'always swing-provider-derived regardless of the active trading mode' (`PortfolioResponse.trading_mode`'s own field description, and `AnalysisResponse`'s equivalent for `as_of`/`extended_data`/`profit_target`). Switching swing mode's own price/signal inputs to IBKR-when-connected would mean two different portfolio snapshots (same account, different moments) could show prices/signals sourced from two different providers depending on IBKR's connection state at request time -- a real product/UX tradeoff (faster loads vs. a potentially confusing source-inconsistency), not a pure performance optimization. This is exactly the kind of judgment call backend-portfolio-load-performance's own description flagged as needing a `decisions` entry with real weighing of the tradeoff, or a `questions`/`waiting_input` escalation if it's genuinely the user's call -- deliberately NOT resolved here in advance, since resolving it meaningfully depends on knowing whether part 1 is even feasible/worth it.

checklist.step: Decide (and record as a `decisions` entry) whether building an IBKR-backed daily/weekly-shaped fetch is worth the added complexity given `get_hourly_bars`' own ~833-day lookback ceiling -- if the resulting history window is judged too short for swing-mode signal quality, say so explicitly and close this task without building it, rather than building a fetch pipeline nobody should actually wire in.

If judged worth building: implement the new IBKR-backed daily/weekly-shaped fetch (a new `IBKRProvider` method or an `app.data.day_trader_intraday`-style resampling adapter over `get_hourly_bars`), with its own hand-computed/reference-value tests per the add-indicator-adjacent data-provider testing convention (no live network calls).

Resolve the swing-vs-IBKR-source tradeoff described above BEFORE wiring the new fetch into `GET /api/portfolio`/`GET /api/portfolio/risk`: either a `decisions` entry with real weighing of the tradeoff (if judged resolvable by the worker), or a `questions` entry + `waiting_input` state (if it's genuinely the user's call) -- do not silently start mixing data sources into swing mode's price/signal fields without that explicit resolution, per the parent task's own description.

PR #352 review finding (backend-portfolio-load-performance): the parent task's own performance investigation measured its '~2N sequential provider round trips' hypothesis with a synthetic fixed-latency (0.05s/call) provider stand-in that never exercised the actual `analyse()` signal-computation code path, so its `decisions` entry's claim that 'No DB-query-pattern or other alternative cause was found to compete with this as the dominant cost' does not hold under realistic conditions. Directly profiling the real, unchanged-by-that-PR per-position `_compute_position_signal` loop against the dev DB's own warm-cache, full-history market data (e.g. AAPL's cached ~11,539-row/~46-year daily history -- a realistic case for any well-established large-cap position, since `YFinanceProvider._fetch` always requests `period='max'`) measured ~32s of CPU-bound `analyse()` computation across a 19-position portfolio (~1.7s/ticker), versus only ~2.7s combined for the now-concurrent price+weekly fetch phases PR #352 optimized -- i.e. once positions include long-history tickers, the sequential signal-computation loop (not the provider round trips PR #352 fixed) is the dominant real-world cost, and PR #352 does not address it, so the underlying 'first load is very very slow' user complaint this whole task chain traces back to is likely still only partially resolved. `cProfile` on a single such `analyse()` call attributed the bulk of the per-ticker cost (~3.5s of ~5.8s) to `app.signals.kangaroo_tail.detect_kangaroo_tails`'s per-bar `_evaluate_candidate` (called once per daily bar -- ~11,528 times for AAPL -- with heavy pandas `.iloc`/`.loc` indexing overhead per call), with `app.signals.divergence.find_divergences`/`app.signals.swing_points.find_swing_points` a smaller but real secondary cost. Recommend: (a) append a `decisions` entry to `docs/tasks/done/backend-portfolio-load-performance.json` (or wherever it lives per `index.json`) caveating/correcting the 'no other cause competes' claim with this finding, and (b) investigate whether `detect_kangaroo_tails` (and the other O(n)-over-full-history signal-engine passes named above) can be vectorized/optimized for realistic full-history daily series, and/or whether the per-position signal-computation loop itself should be parallelized -- noting it's CPU-bound, so a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (GIL-bound) wouldn't help the way it does for I/O; a `ProcessPoolExecutor` or an algorithmic fix would be needed instead.

PR #352 review finding (backend-portfolio-load-performance): that parent task's `decisions` entry states that extending `GET /api/portfolio/risk`'s own sequential per-position `get_weekly_ohlcv` loop (in `app/api/routers/portfolio.py`'s `get_risk`) to an analogous concurrent-fetch-the-survivors treatment was 'left as a candidate for the backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups task created alongside this one' -- but this follow-up task's own checklist, as originally filed, didn't actually contain that candidate anywhere (this entry is that omission being corrected). If picked up: `get_risk`'s loop deliberately interleaves a cheap, no-network filter (`_stop_and_filtered_daily`/`protective_stop`) with the weekly fetch specifically so a position that fails the cheap check never pays for a weekly round trip that would be thrown away -- naively prefetching weekly data for every swing position up front (mirroring `_prefetch_swing_weekly_ohlcv`'s shape) would defeat that existing optimization, so a proper fix needs its own two-phase (cheap-filter-then-concurrently-fetch-the-survivors) design, not a direct copy of `_prefetch_swing_weekly_ohlcv`.

decisions.decision:
Building an IBKR-backed daily/weekly-shaped fetch is judged NOT worth it, so this task closes checklist items 1-3 without building or wiring anything new -- `current_price`/`equity`/swing signal inputs stay exactly as they are today ('always swing-provider-derived regardless of trading mode', `PortfolioResponse.trading_mode`'s own field description), completely untouched. Rejected the description's own framing that the resampled series' history would be too short to CLEAR THE MINIMUM: `docs/Analyse.md` §8's own stated 'Data Requirements' is 'daily OHLCV history (minimum ~200 trading days, to seed 26-week/weekly EMA & MACD after resampling)', and `IBKRProvider.max_lookback_days_for_bar_size('1h')` (the pagination-bound ceiling `get_hourly_bars` already self-limits to) is ~833 calendar days -- roughly 570-595 trading days after weekends/holidays, comfortably above that 200-day floor and also above the ~100-week (~700-calendar-day) floor `docs/Analyse.md` separately cites for a fresh-entry `profit_target` candidate to even have a chance of forming. So an IBKR-resampled daily/weekly fetch would in fact clear this app's own documented bare-minimum signal-computability bar, contrary to what this task's own `description` worried about.

But clearing the bare minimum isn't the real question. Two independent findings make building it not worth it anyway: (1) yfinance/Stooq's own `period='max'` fetch routinely returns FAR more history than that 200-day minimum for any established ticker -- the parent task's own profiling used AAPL's real cached ~11,539-row/~46-year daily history as its realistic test case. An IBKR-resampled fetch capped at ~570-595 daily bars would be a ~20x reduction in available history for such a position, degrading exactly the whole-history-dependent computations that read well beyond the bare EMA/MACD warm-up: `app.signals.support_resistance.detect_support_resistance_zones`'s whole-history swing-point clustering (feeds `profit_target`), `app.signals.divergence.find_divergences`'s multi-year swing-point-based divergence detection, and `app.portfolio.grading.grade_trade_from_filtered_history`'s own history-length gate (a trade grade already degrades to null when 'the ticker's fetched daily history doesn't reach back to the entry/exit date', docs/Analyse.md §6) -- a position/trade entered more than ~2.3 years ago would silently regress from a real target/grade to null the moment IBKR-sourced data replaced yfinance/Stooq's for it, a real signal-quality regression even though the bare 200-day floor is cleared. (2) This task's own checklist item 4 finding (see the corresponding `decisions` entry below) independently confirms that provider round trips are NOT the dominant cost of a realistic full-history portfolio load once backend-portfolio-load-performance's own concurrency fix (PR #352) is in place -- CPU-bound signal computation is. Building an IBKR-backed fetch to solve a 'provider round trips are the bottleneck' problem that measurement has already falsified would add real, ongoing complexity (a new fetch/resample pipeline, its own tests, an available-history regression for established positions) for no measurable improvement on the actual, now-dominant cost -- if anything, an IBKR-sourced fetch's own drastically shorter history would make `detect_kangaroo_tails`/`find_divergences` spuriously faster over ~570 bars instead of ~11,539, but only as an accidental byproduct of having much less real history to look at, not because the underlying signal-computation loop's per-bar cost improved at all.

Rejected alternative: building it anyway on the theory that clearing the 200-day minimum is sufficient justification -- rejected because that minimum is a floor for basic signal COMPUTABILITY (can Screen 1's weekly EMA/MACD even be seeded at all), not evidence that swing signal QUALITY (support/resistance zone strength and count, divergence detection depth, trade-grading history reach) is unaffected by a ~20x-shorter available window, and because it wouldn't address the now-confirmed actual bottleneck anyway.
decisions.rationale: The parent task's own description explicitly asked this follow-up to weigh both parts (build-worthiness, then source-tradeoff) rather than assume either answer -- this resolves part 1 with genuine measurement-backed reasoning (docs/Analyse.md's own documented minimum, cross-checked against the parent task's own real AAPL-history profiling, cross-checked against this task's own re-confirmation that provider round trips are no longer the dominant cost) rather than restating the description's own unverified worry about the minimum not being cleared.

decisions.decision: Because checklist item 1 concluded the IBKR-backed fetch is not worth building at all, checklist item 3's premise (a live swing-vs-IBKR-source tradeoff to resolve before wiring anything in) does not arise -- there is nothing to wire in, so no `decisions` entry weighing that tradeoff or `questions`/`waiting_input` escalation is needed. This mirrors the exact resolution pattern the parent task's own decisions entry already used for its own checklist item 4 (a hypothetical about a capability that doesn't exist can't be meaningfully answered, so it isn't escalated to a `questions` entry) -- see that entry (docs/tasks/done/backend-portfolio-load-performance.json) for the identical reasoning applied one level up.
decisions.rationale: Escalating a hypothetical 'which source should swing mode prefer' question to `questions`/`waiting_input` when no such capability is being built would stall this task on a question with no actionable answer today -- consistent with the parent task's own precedent for the same shape of non-question.

decisions.decision: Appended a new `decisions` entry to `docs/tasks/done/backend-portfolio-load-performance.json` (not an in-place edit of its existing entry's text) correcting the 'No DB-query-pattern or other alternative cause was found to compete with this as the dominant cost' claim, per checklist item 4's own recommendation (a). Independently re-confirmed the underlying finding myself before writing the correction, rather than taking PR #352's review/pr_decision numbers on faith: profiled `app.signals.kangaroo_tail.detect_kangaroo_tails` directly (not the full `analyse()` pipeline) against a synthetic ~11,539-row daily series (matching AAPL's cited real history length, since a live network fetch isn't available in this sandboxed environment) with `cProfile` -- measured ~1.67-1.8s wall-clock for a single such call, matching the ~1.7s/ticker figure PR #352's review and pr_decision both independently arrived at via their own separate methods (this task's own third independent measurement, converging on the same order of magnitude).
decisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md's task-board convention: correcting a stale claim inside an already-`done` task's existing `decisions` entry defaults to appending a brand-new array entry (not amending the existing entry's text in place) unless the correction is a narrow factual fix the task's own checklist explicitly calls out the existing entry's text as the thing to fix -- neither applies here (this is a substantive correction to a conclusion, not a narrow fact, and no checklist item names the existing entry's own text), so the append-only default was used. Re-measuring myself (rather than only citing PR #352's own numbers) matches this codebase's established convention of not trusting a prior measurement without independently reproducing it -- the same standard `pr-decision` itself already applied when it independently re-profiled the same function against its own synthetic series before confirming PR #352's accept.

decisions.decision: Investigated checklist item 4's recommendation (b) (whether `detect_kangaroo_tails` can be vectorized, and/or whether the per-position signal-computation loop should be parallelized) but did NOT implement either fix in this task -- instead prototyped a vectorized `detect_kangaroo_tails` equivalent (pandas `.shift`/`.rolling(lookback)` replacing the per-bar window slice + `.mean()`/`.max()`/`.min()`, `np.where` replacing the per-bar direction/retracement branching) and validated it against the SAME synthetic ~11,539-row fixture used for the CPU-bound re-profiling above: identical tail set (60/60 matching `(date, direction)` pairs, including the up-priority outside-bar tie-break) at a measured ~450x wall-clock speedup (1.80s -> 0.004s for one ticker's full history). This is strong evidence a vectorized rewrite is both feasible and high-payoff, but shipping it was judged out of scope for THIS task: it needs its own hand-computed reference-value tests per this codebase's `add-indicator` convention (parity against the old implementation on one synthetic fixture is evidence of feasibility, not the rigor this codebase requires for a change to core signal-detection math -- see `backend-kangaroo-tail-pattern.json`'s own original decisions for the book-derived thresholds/tie-breaks a rewrite must independently reproduce, not just numerically match), plus `verify-elder-signal` review given it directly gates SELL/BUY confidence. Filed `docs/tasks/backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups.json` (depends_on this task, skill: add-indicator) to carry this investigation's findings (including the working prototype approach) forward as its own properly-scoped task, alongside the `ProcessPoolExecutor`-based per-position-parallelization alternative checklist item 4 also named (noted there as CPU-bound work a `ThreadPoolExecutor` genuinely cannot help with, unlike this task's own I/O-bound provider-fetch fixes) -- did not attempt to also profile `find_divergences`/`find_swing_points` in equal depth (time-boxed this investigation to the already-identified dominant single function); left as an explicit checklist item on the new follow-up task instead.
decisions.rationale: A full production vectorization rewrite of core pattern-detection math is qualitatively different work from this task's other three checklist items (an investigation, a documentation correction, and an I/O-concurrency fix reusing an already-established pattern) -- it's genuinely `add-indicator`-governed work needing its own dedicated reference-value tests and elder-signal-methodology review, the same bar `backend-kangaroo-tail-pattern`'s original implementation was held to, not something to slip into a broader 'followups' task's own checklist alongside three much narrower items. Filing a new tracked task (rather than leaving this only as a comment) follows this same task's own originating precedent (the parent backend-portfolio-load-performance task filing this task itself, for the identical reason: real out-of-scope work discovered mid-investigation shouldn't be silently either done under-scrutinized or dropped).

decisions.decision: Implemented checklist item 5: `GET /api/portfolio/risk`'s swing-mode branch of its first-pass loop is now a genuine two-phase design, mirroring `GET /api/portfolio`'s own `_prefetch_swing_weekly_ohlcv` concurrency pattern WITHOUT copying its shape directly (which would have defeated this endpoint's own pre-existing optimization -- see below). Phase (a) resolves `protective_stop`/`_stop_and_filtered_daily` for every swing position from data already fetched (`e.daily_ohlcv`) -- a pure, no-network computation, exactly as before. Phase (b) then fetches `get_weekly_ohlcv` CONCURRENTLY, but only for phase (a)'s survivors, via a new shared helper `_fetch_weekly_ohlcv_concurrently(tickers, provider)` extracted from `_prefetch_swing_weekly_ohlcv`'s own inline `ThreadPoolExecutor` fan-out (that function now just resolves its own ticker list and delegates to the shared helper, so both call sites' identical concurrency shape has exactly one implementation, not two hand-kept-in-sync copies). The day-trader-mode branch is unchanged (its own legs were already fetched concurrently, up front, via `fetch_day_trader_legs_concurrently`) -- it's now its own separate `if day_trader_active: ... else: ...` sub-loop rather than interleaved with the swing branch inside one shared loop, since the two branches no longer share an inline weekly-fetch call site to interleave around. Added a genuinely discriminating regression test (`test_weekly_fetch_outcome_not_swapped_when_completion_order_differs_from_submission_order`, tests/integration/test_portfolio_risk.py) using a new `_DelayedWeeklyStubProvider` fixture (mirroring `test_portfolio_get.py`'s own `_DelayedWeeklyProvider`): the first-submitted ticker (AAPL, earlier `entry_date`) is deliberately the slowest to complete and fails, while the second-submitted (MSFT) finishes first and succeeds -- manually mutation-tested by temporarily swapping the shared helper's `future.result() for future in futures.items()` gather for an `as_completed(...)`-based one, confirming BOTH this new test AND `test_portfolio_get.py`'s own pre-existing `test_weekly_prefetch_outcome_not_swapped_when_completion_order_differs_from_submission_order` failed (since both call sites now share the same helper), then reverting. Also added `test_position_with_failed_swing_price_fetch_is_excluded_in_day_trader_mode` to restore 100% branch coverage on the day-trader branch's own (now separately located) `e.position.current_price is None` guard, which the refactor's loop split left uncovered by the existing day-trader-mode test fixtures (none of which combined day-trader mode with a failed swing-side price fetch before).
decisions.rationale: A naive fix (calling `_prefetch_swing_weekly_ohlcv` directly from `get_risk`, or inlining an equivalent 'fetch weekly for every swing position up front') was rejected: it would prefetch weekly data for every enriched swing position regardless of whether that position's own daily-side `protective_stop` computation would even succeed, defeating `get_risk`'s own pre-existing, explicitly-documented 'don't pay for a weekly round trip that would be thrown away' optimization (already covered by `test_daily_excluded_position_never_triggers_weekly_fetch`, which still passes unchanged) for any position that fails the cheap daily-side filter -- exactly the risk this task's own checklist item 5 wording flagged. Extracting the shared `_fetch_weekly_ohlcv_concurrently` helper (rather than duplicating the `ThreadPoolExecutor` fan-out inline in `get_risk`) was chosen over leaving two independent copies: this codebase's own established precedent (`backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups`'s `compute_day_trader_signals_concurrently` pattern reused, not reimplemented, by every later concurrent-fetch task) favors one shared implementation over duplicated near-identical concurrency shapes, and the parent task's own `decisions` entry already flagged the two independent inline copies it would otherwise have produced across `pricing.py`/`portfolio.py` as a discretionary tradeoff a reviewer might weigh differently -- this task takes the opportunity to resolve that within `portfolio.py`'s own two call sites (the `pricing.py` one stays separate, since it's a different function -- price fetch, not weekly OHLCV -- in a different architectural layer, per that same entry's own layering rationale).

comments.summary: Non-blocking: `_fetch_weekly_ohlcv_concurrently`'s docstring claims a duplicate ticker is 'fetched at most once', but `{ticker: executor.submit(_fetch, ticker) for ticker in tickers}` actually re-submits/re-executes `_fetch` once per occurrence (verified independently: 3-item list with one repeat produced 3 calls, not 2) -- only the stored future per key is deduplicated to the last submission. Pre-existing behavior inherited unchanged from `_prefetch_swing_weekly_ohlcv`'s prior inline code (which never made this claim), and currently unreachable given `PositionORM.ticker`'s DB-level `unique=True` constraint (no two positions can share a ticker today). Tracked as a checklist entry on `backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups` (already existed, still planned) rather than a new follow-up task.

review.notes: Independently verified every claim in the task-worker's own report rather than trusting it: (1) read docs/Analyse.md §8 directly -- the ~200-trading-day minimum claim is accurate; independently computed IBKRProvider.max_lookback_days_for_bar_size('1h') = 20 pages * 1000 bars/page * 1h = 833.33 calendar days, ~595 trading days at a naive 5/7 ratio -- comfortably clears the 200-day floor, confirming the PR's arithmetic and its correction of the parent task's own framing. (2) Independently re-profiled app.signals.kangaroo_tail.detect_kangaroo_tails with cProfile against a synthetic ~11,539-row daily series (matching AAPL's real cached history length) -- measured 1.71s wall-clock for one call, matching the PR's claimed 1.7-1.8s/ticker range and PR #352's own converging figures; read _evaluate_candidate's implementation and confirm its O(n) per-bar re-slicing/pandas-indexing shape plausibly explains this cost. (3) Diffed docs/tasks/done/backend-portfolio-load-performance.json's decisions array against main -- confirmed genuinely append-only (original two entries byte-unchanged, one new entry appended with its own timestamp/rationale). (4) Mutation-tested _fetch_weekly_ohlcv_concurrently myself: swapped the submission-order gather for an as_completed(...)-based one, confirmed both the new test_weekly_fetch_outcome_not_swapped_when_completion_order_differs_from_submission_order and the pre-existing test_portfolio_get.py concurrency test failed, then reverted (working tree confirmed clean after revert). (5) Read the new backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups task filed for the vectorization prototype -- confirmed its own checklist correctly identifies 'matches old implementation on one synthetic fixture' as feasibility evidence only, not the hand-computed-reference-value rigor add-indicator/verify-elder-signal require, and requires that rigor before any future shipment; deferring is sound. (6) Judged the 'not worth building IBKR fetch' decision a genuinely resolvable engineering call (grounded in measured facts: ~20x-shorter history degrading signal quality, and provider round trips no longer being the dominant cost at all) rather than a product ambiguity needing user escalation -- checklist item 3's premise (which source swing mode should prefer) never arises once item 1 concludes nothing new is being built, and the task's own decisions entries walk through this correctly. (7) Re-ran the full backend suite (1456 passed), coverage (100%, gate 90%), ruff/mypy (clean), check_profit_target_wording.py (clean), validate_tasks.py (clean, both before and after adding my own follow-up checklist entry), and confirmed `python scripts/export_openapi.py` produces zero diff against the committed backend/openapi.json (genuinely a no-op, no route/schema touched). No frontend files are touched by this PR and no user-facing behavior changed (GET /api/portfolio/risk's response shape/filtering semantics are unchanged, only its internal fetch concurrency) -- browser walkthrough and the e2e-test skill are both skipped as genuinely inapplicable, not omitted. No new module/dependency/layer is introduced (a function extracted into a shared private helper within an existing router file), so architecture-review wasn't run. No signal/confidence/risk math shipped in this diff (the vectorization prototype was investigated but explicitly not shipped), so a full verify-elder-signal pass wasn't run either -- the §8 data-requirements claim was independently checked directly instead, per this review's own step 1. One minor non-blocking documentation-accuracy finding filed against the existing backend-portfolio-load-performance-followups-followups follow-up task rather than a new one.
